name: image-trail
summary: Five copies of one panel stacked in a single grid cell, each lerping toward the pointer at its own rate so the panel smears into a trail while you move and closes back up when you stop.

total.description: How many copies make up the trail. Upstream's totalTrailElements.

travel.description: Pixels the trail swings either side of centre across the section. Upstream's valuesFromTo x/y bound.

deviations.what: The trail copies are divs painted from the --fx-image custom property, not tags whose src is parsed out of the host element's inline background-image.
deviations.why: Codrops ships the demo's photographs under separate terms and this library redistributes none of them. The default is a layered gradient that makes the trail legible on its own, and a site author points --fx-image at their own picture with one declaration. Upstream's bgImage regex, the opacityChange option and the perspective branch go with it, since all three exist to configure that .

deviations.what: The pointer is measured against the section's own box rather than against window.innerWidth / innerHeight, the listener is on the section rather than on window, and the cursor therefore starts at the normalised centre 0.5 where upstream starts at winsize.width/2.
deviations.why: The sketch owns its whole page. An effect is one section among several and a page may carry this one twice, so window-relative tracking would have both trails answering to the other's half of the screen.

deviations.what: The rotation axes are dropped: valuesFromTo rx, ry and rz, the perspective option and the rotateX/rotateY/rotateZ terms of the transform string.
deviations.why: All three ranges are [0, 0] in the sketch this port pins, so they contribute the identity rotation on every frame. Sketches 006 to 010 are where they carry values, and those are separate ports.

deviations.what: The render loop is cancelled on destroy and the stack's original markup is restored.
deviations.why: Upstream recurses through requestAnimationFrame forever, because its page never tears the sketch down. Here a destroy would otherwise leave a loop writing transforms into detached nodes on every frame for the life of the tab.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion no copies are built and no loop starts.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest. The stylesheet's resting panel is the finished content, and a stack that chases the pointer is the exact motion this visitor asked not to have.
